desc: Analyze the problem and note that the graph of immediate right/left neighbors is a forest of trees (Hasse diagram of the interval order).
Prove that any shortest path in the original disjointness graph can be replaced by a path that only uses immediate right/left neighbors (i.e., the forest suffices).
Build the forest: for each vertex, find its immediate right neighbor (first with L > R_i) and immediate left neighbor (last with R < L_i) using binary search on sorted arrays.
Determine connected components (trees) in the forest using union-find or BFS.
For each tree, precompute prefix sums of weights along root-to-leaf paths so that the path weight between any two vertices in the same tree can be computed in O(1) using LCA.
Answer each query: if s and t are in different trees, print -1; else compute the path weight as W_s + W_t + sum of weights of vertices on the path excluding s and t, using LCA.
Test the implementation on the provided sample inputs and additional cases (including the counterexample) to verify correctness.
Optimize for time and memory limits (O(N log N) for sorting and binary search, O(N) for tree construction, O(1) per query after O(N log N) preprocessing).
